newsitem.title: USA: USDA lays out rules for new conservation program.
newsitem.headline: USDA lays out rules for new conservation program.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Friday laid out proposed rules for the new $1.3 billion Environmental Quality Incentives Program (EQIP).

The seven-year program, created under the 1996 Farm Bill, would provide cost-share money, incentive payments and expert advice to farmers and ranchers who want to make environmental and conservation improvements. Half the money is earmarked for livestock farmers.
USDA said it is seeking public comment on the rules through Nov. 25 and that public meetings will be held Oct. 11-21 across the country to discuss the program.
Agriculture Department Secretary Dan Glickman encouraged comment on the proposed rules.
"We want to ensure we begin with the best program possible that benefits everyone," he said in a statement.

Under the proposed rules, EQIP would offer five-to-10 year contracts. USDA said total cost-share and incentive payments would be limited to $10,000 per person per year and $50,000 over the length of a contract.

USDA would provide cost share assistance for up to 75 percent of the costs of certain conservation practices on family-sized farms and ranches. Large livestock operations would not be eligible for cost-share aid for animal waste management facilities.
The department said incentives payments would be up to 100 percent of the producer's costs for up to three years.
USDA said applications would be accepted throughout the year but that offers would be ranked and selected during designated periods.
It said outreach efforts were being made to ensure all eligible producers had access to the program.
EQUIP replaces four previous conservation programs.
